english.title: Distributor supplying new EEE fail to make information available to private household user

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: the Waste Electrical and electronic equipment regulations 2013

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a distributor who supplied new EEE, failed to make information available in writing to a user of EEE in a private household, namely **(..SPECIFY USER..), on

(A)_[the requirement on each Member State under Article 5(1) of Directive 2012/19/EU of the European Parliament to minimise the disposal of WEEE as unsorted municipal waste and to achieve a high level of collection of WEEE for treatment, recovery and environmentally sound disposal]_
(B)_[the collection and take-back systems that were available to him]_
(C)_[the collection and take-back systems that were available to her]_
(D)_[his role in contributing to the reuse, recycling and other forms of recovery of WEEE under the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013]_
(E)_[her role in contributing to the reuse, recycling and other forms of recovery of WEEE under the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013]_
(F)_[the potential effects on the environment and human health as a result of the presence of hazardous substances in EEE]_
(G)_[the meaning of the crossed out wheeled bin symbol shown in Schedule 6 to the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013]_
(H)_[**(..SPECIFY COMBINATION OF ABOVE..)]_
english.legislation: Contrary to regulations 44, 90(6) and 91(2) of the Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment Regulations 2013.
